about: Which namespaces a name names, and which types a link to one leads to: the namespace's own first, then those of the namespaces under it, nested types included and members not, as Magnus agreed (2026-11-26).
Cloyd's chat and the .NET Terminal Symbol Linker link names alike, and both are checked against these cases: Cloyd by Finding_the_types_of_a_namespace, the symbol linker by TypesOfNamespacesTest.

This file is the original, in ~/.claude at src/Cloyd.Specifications/Links/CasesSharedWithTheSymbolLinker. The symbol linker keeps a copy in its test resources, and its tests fail while the copy differs from it.
declarations: what each namespace declares, each type with its members' names and the types nested in it. A namespace without a name is the global one.
typesANameLeadsTo: each case's name, as a text writes it, and the qualified names of the types a link to the namespaces it names leads to, in order.
namesOfNamespaces: each case's names, as a text writes them, and whether each names a namespace.

typesANameLeadsTo.case: a namespace has its own types first, then those of the namespaces under it, and not their members
typesANameLeadsTo.name: Shop.Orders

typesANameLeadsTo.case: a namespace with no types of its own has those of the namespaces under it
typesANameLeadsTo.name: Shop

typesANameLeadsTo.case: the end of a namespace's name leads to its types
typesANameLeadsTo.name: Orders.Shipping

namesOfNamespaces.case: a namespace's name and each of its ends name it
part of a name in it, a name left out, or a type after it name none
